context.title: Two Unfaithful Sisters
context.summary: Samaria (Aholah) and Jerusalem (Aholibah) are pictured as two sisters who sell themselves to Egypt, Assyria and Babylon; Jerusalem, having seen her sister's fate, behaves even worse.
context.background: The names seem to mean 'her tent' and 'my tent is in her,' hinting at worship and God's dwelling. The allegory concerns politics as much as religion: the kings of Israel and Judah sought security in alliances with empires, adopting their gods. The northern kingdom fell to Assyria in 722 BC, which should have been a warning to Judah.
watchFor: Jerusalem is condemned for not learning from Samaria (v. 11).
The 'cup' of her sister's judgment passed to her (vv. 31–34).
The recurring list of three powers: Egypt, Assyria, Babylon.

people.name: Aholibah
people.summary: My tent is in her, the name of an imaginary harlot, applied symbolically to Jerusalem, because she had abandoned the worship of the true God and given herself up to the idolatries of foreign nations.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Samaria
places.summary: A watch-mountain or a watch-tower. In the heart of the mountains of Israel, a few miles north-west of Shechem, stands the “hill of Shomeron,” a solitary mountain, a great “mamelon.”

places.name: Assyria
places.summary: The name derived from the city Asshur on the Tigris, the original capital of the country, was originally a colony from Babylonia, and was ruled by viceroys from that kingdom.

places.name: Chaldea
places.summary: The southern portion of Babylonia, Lower Mesopotamia, lying chiefly on the right bank of the Euphrates, but commonly used of the whole of the Mesopotamian plain.

places.name: Koa
places.summary: He-camel, occurs only in Ezek. 23:23, some province or place in the Babylonian empire, used in this passage along with Shoa.

places.name: Pekod
places.summary: Probably a place in Babylonia (Jer. 50:21; Ezek. 23:23).

places.name: Shoa
places.summary: Opulent, the mountain district lying to the north-east of Babylonia, anciently the land of the Guti, or Kuti, the modern Kurdistan. The plain lying between these mountains and the Tigris was called su-Edina, i.e., “the border of the plain.”

events.title: Prophecies of Ezekiel
events.summary: Passage: Ezekiel 1:1–48:35. People: Ezekiel. Lasted about 23 years.
